law: Neither Animal nor Beastman nor quite a Devil, old enough that no one agrees which category it actually belongs to. D&D class: Sorcerer, Draconic Bloodline.
The paired opposite of Anchor, letting something slip slowly from where it's supposed to be. D&D class: Sorcerer, Wild Magic.
The paired opposite of Wet, and closer kin to Earth than to anything from Undine. D&D class: — a state modifier, not a class.
A sibling tier to the Death knight, just as demanding about needing a strong, high level corpse, but bound to ride rather than walk and to carry its own head rather than wear it.
The narrow seam between Day and Night, too brief for most to bother claiming. D&D class: Cleric, Twilight Domain.

Earth is the law that is formed from the corpse of Gnome the spirit of Earth, part of the power that comes from the Spirit Realm , the power hold more power to those more attuned to the spirit like those of the spiritual bloodline like Shaman and Elves. D&D class: Sorcerer, Gnome Bloodline. Like eve
The opposite instinct to Redundancy, a Mechanical law of doing more with less rather than protecting against failure. D&D class: Artificer, Armorer.
A splinter that sits closer to Pride than to either Light or Dark outright. D&D class: Fighter, Cavalier.
The paired opposite of anything rigid, letting a shape bend under a hit instead of breaking. D&D class: Artificer, Armorer.
A cousin of Lightning, smaller in scale and far easier for a mortal to reach without a god's blood behind it. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Storm Herald (Sea).
A splinter of Light that carries someone else's feeling rather than one's own. D&D class: Cleric, Peace Domain.
A Void law of absent space, Zero's cousin, describing nothing where something should be. D&D class: Monk, Way of Shadow.
The practice of binding a Law directly into an object rather than a person, letting even those without godhood or bloodline wield a sliver of it. D&D class: Wizard, School of Enchantment.
The paired opposite of Beginning, though unlike Death it belongs to the Void rather than to Infinatas. D&D class: — an abstract/definitional concept, not a class.
The broader, slower cousin of End, describing a whole thing winding down rather than one moment stopping. D&D class: — a descriptive modifier of End, not its own class.
One of the Cosmic powers like Plasma, the raw capacity to do anything at all before it's shaped into something more specific. D&D class: Sorcerer, Clockwork Soul.
The Void's slow law of things falling apart on their own, without needing Destruction to help. D&D class: Cleric, Death Domain.
One of the Original Sin cluster, a splinter of Dark shaped by wanting what someone else has rather than what's simply gone. D&D class: Warlock, The Genie.
Undine wearing down Gnome one grain at a time, patient in a way Lava and Storm never are. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Land.
What's left of a Spirit or god once even its Laws have been stripped away — nothing usable, just proof it existed. D&D class: — inert by definition, no class draws on it.
Claimed by almost nothing, since even Infinatas wasn't always a god and nothing about the Void is guaranteed to last. D&D class: — reserved; near mythical, claimed by nothing currently.

A slower, permanent cousin of Transformation, changing something for good instead of just for a moment. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Moon.
The Void's broadest law, the simple fact of being real — opposed only by Deletion. D&D class: Cleric, Order Domain.
Paired opposite of Success, and the more common outcome for anyone reaching past their Aptitude. D&D class: — the common default outcome, not something wielded as a class.
The plain, unshaped end of anything Flight briefly interrupted. D&D class: — a plain physical outcome, not a class.
The root Law under Illusion and Lies both, rarely used on its own since it needs something else to lie about. D&D class: Wizard, School of Illusion.
A splinter shaped by the Mortal Realm noticing someone, not clearly kin to Light or Dark since it depends entirely on how the notice is used. D&D class: Bard, College of Swords.

Fear is its own entity, formed when Dark was siphoned down to raw dread instead, sharper and faster to act than what became Sadness. D&D class: Warlock, The Fiend (official subclass, reflavored so the patron is Fear itself rather than a devil).
A rarer, unstable result — a corpse caught halfway between the summon and the original's actual return, holding power unpredictably rather than in any fixed share.
The paired opposite of Hollow, though what actually fills the space depends entirely on what's doing the filling. D&D class: Cleric, Life Domain.
A Void law describing a limit, the boundary Infinite refuses to have. D&D class: — an abstract boundary concept, not a class.
The paired opposite of Last, claimed constantly and rarely for long. D&D class: — an abstract ordinal concept, not a class.
A narrower version of Stabilise, meant for objects and wounds rather than whole spells. D&D class: Artificer, Battle Smith.
The part of a Corpse that Decay claims first, before Bones. D&D class: — a material, covered by the Undead Summoning system.
Borrowed more often from Air or Sylph's children than earned any other way. D&D class: Sorcerer, bloodline to Sylph.
A small Void law, swapping one state for its opposite without touching anything else about it. D&D class: — a minor utility modifier, not a class.
What Bloom leaves behind, prized by Alchemy as much as by anyone chasing Charm. D&D class: — a natural product, not a class.
The paired opposite of Friend, and the easier of the two to fake. D&D class: — a relational status, not a class.
The practice of arranging several Laws together in a pattern, since some effects — like Vortex or Apocalypse — only work when more than one Law lines up correctly. D&D class: Wizard, War Magic.
The paired opposite of Decay in its earliest, gentlest form, closer to Preserve than to full Regeneration. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
Paired opposite of Foe, and the harder of the two Laws to use honestly. D&D class: — a relational status, not a class.
The act of combining two Laws the way Vortex combined Sylph and Spin. D&D class: Sorcerer, Clockwork Soul.
One face of Time, harder to bend than Past since nothing has happened yet to bend. D&D class: Wizard, School of Divination.
A Gamble made on purpose as an opening move, rather than out of desperation. D&D class: Fighter, Battle Master.
A Ghoul made worse by rotting on tainted ground instead of ordinary soil, stronger for it and carrying a stench potent enough to work as a weapon on its own.

A step above Skeleton, made from a corpse only partway through Decay rather than bare Bones, holding onto around a tenth of the original's power along with a predator's cunning instead of nothing at all.
The willing version of Take, power or Life handed over rather than pulled. D&D class: Cleric, Life Domain.
The counterpart to Boy, and just as tied to Youth rather than to any Law. D&D class: — a category, not a class.
A shape that trades Dagger's speed for Spear's reach and neither shape's balance. D&D class: Fighter, Purple Dragon Knight.
Another of the Original Sin cluster, Desire that never recognizes when it's been satisfied. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Beast.

Gnome is the spirit of Earth, one of the progenitors dwelling in the Spirit Realm before its corpse became the Earth Law. Not the small folk of the same name — an entity of stone and root that predates them by an age, said to have been slow moving, patient to the point of stillness, and utterly with

progTitle: the Twin-Faced Shade of God-Specific Runes
law: Not a Law but a category: Runes that only one god holds, either because that god was never broken apart or because it took every piece of a dead god for itself. Infinatas, one of the last original gods, still holds Laws no one else can reach, because they were never pulled from a corpse: Life and De
A ranking mortals invented to measure Aptitude, meaningless to the gods the Laws actually come from. D&D class: — a mortal ranking, not a class.

Gravity is its own entity, formed when the Void's own weightlessness was siphoned against itself until it started pulling inward instead of drifting. D&D class: Wizard, Graviturgy Magic (official subclass).
The last of the common Original Sin cluster, close kin to Envy but wanting more rather than wanting someone else's. D&D class: Bard, College of Swords.
A slower cousin of Sadness, less a splinter of Dark than the ash left after one burns out. D&D class: Cleric, Twilight Domain.

progTitle: the Shrouded Shade of Grim Reaper
law: Not something a necromancer summons at all, but a role an undead grows into after collecting enough deaths on its own, sitting above every deliberate summon on this list.
The paired opposite of Uncertain, usable only once every variable involved is already known. D&D class: Wizard, School of Divination.
A Law that rewards repetition, growing stronger the more predictably it's used and weaker the one time it isn't. D&D class: — a meta mechanic, not a class.
Rain caught mid fall by Frost, hard enough to bruise before it ever reaches the ground. D&D class: Ranger, Hunter.
A visible symptom of Divinity, worn more as proof than as any power of its own. D&D class: — a cosmetic marker, not a class.
A sharper, shorter lived cousin of Speed, burning out faster than it lasts. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Drunken Master.
The hardened, lasting form Anger takes once it stops burning and starts settling, closer kin to Scorn than to Dark itself. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Berserker.
The mortal, bloodline free measure of how much Life a body is currently holding onto. D&D class: — a resource/stat, not a class.
A refined sense, second only to Vision in how often Martial cultivators bother training it. D&D class: — a trained sense, not a class of its own.
Where a body is said to keep whatever Life it's holding, which is why losing it ends things faster than any other wound. D&D class: — an anatomical concept, not a class.
What's left of Love once Sadness gets to it. D&D class: Bard, College of Spirits.

Heat is its own entity, formed when only the barest sliver of Fire was siphoned off by itself, too thin to carry any of Ignis's real shape but a distinct being all the same. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Four Elements, reflavored so every technique draws only on Heat rather than all four elements at o
The Nature adjacent raw material most Alchemy starts from, before any Law shapes it further. D&D class: — a raw material, not a class.
Paired opposite of Fill, describing what's left once Essence has already been taken. D&D class: Monk, Way of Shadow.
A sibling to Happiness under Light, reaching toward something rather than resting in it. D&D class: Cleric, Life Domain.

The Law of horns: the body growing its own weapon from bone. A body Law like Muscle and Breath, it lets anything with a skull push something hard and sharp out of it, and it's why horned creatures heal their horns when nothing else about them heals. In practice it's a Law of charging and goring. Hor
A blood drinking variant that doesn't lose power the way Skeleton or Zombie do, so long as it keeps feeding on Blood to make up for what Decay keeps trying to take.
The plainest offensive Law on record, doing exactly what it says without any shape or element behind it. D&D class: Fighter, Champion.
A changed form of the Water power that had been extracted from Undine dying corpse. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
What a Sin or a virtue looks like before a mortal actually acts on it. D&D class: — an abstract concept, not a class.
Used to tell a Friend from a Foe, or a real god from one wearing a stolen Law. D&D class: Wizard, School of Divination.

Ignis is the spirit of Fire, one of the progenitors who lived in the Spirit Realm before its corpse became the Fire Law. The old records describe it as hungry rather than cruel: it consumed whatever it touched because that was all it knew how to do, and it gave off warmth as freely as it destroyed.
Built from False the way Fire is built from Ignis — a Law with an origin no one living has met. D&D class: Wizard, School of Illusion.
A copy of appearance only, thinner than Illusion since it doesn't fool anything but sight. D&D class: Wizard, School of Illusion.
A narrower, permanent version of Resistance, earned rather than cast. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Long Death.
The combination of Cage and Chain together, strong enough to hold something with real power rather than just a person. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
A cousin of Boost, slower to apply but longer lasting. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of Glory.

Inane is Infinatas's split personality: the same being, turned the other way. Where Infinatas keeps the balance of existence through Creation, Inane keeps it through Destruction. D&D class: none. Inane tier power is reserved and not something a player character starts with. Infinatas is the creator
The opposite of Direct, trading accuracy for reach or spread. D&D class: — a modifier, not a class.

progTitle: the Creator of All, the Balance Itself
law: Infinatas is one of the last original gods: not a replica built from dead gods' Runes, but a god who was never killed and never usurped. Even so, he wasn't always a god (see God). What he was before is not recorded. Because he was never broken apart, Infinatas still holds Laws no one else can: Life
The absence of any edge Finite would draw, one of the Void's more dangerous abstractions to hold. D&D class: Sorcerer, Aberrant Mind.
How Royalty, Legacy, and sometimes a Law itself pass from one generation to the next. D&D class: — a narrative/legal concept, not a class.
The paired opposite of Tradition, and the rarer of the two to be trusted right away. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Artificer class generally, not a subclass of its own.
A Law meant to provoke rather than harm directly, often paired with Anger or Rage. D&D class: Bard, College of Whispers.
The trait tied to how much a mind can hold and combine, most useful to those who chase Alchemy or Knowledge. D&D class: — an ability score, not a class.

Dark's answer to both Empathy and Belonging, cutting the thread either would need. D&D class: Monk, Way of Shadow.
